A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a crosscut fissur carbide bur at high speed (20,000 rpm) produced a high bond strength, and a fine straight fissure diamond at low speed (20, 000 rpm) was the least effective bur for bonding composite restorations.
the bond strength achieved with the crosscut fissure bur was significantly higher than the bond strength achieved by the fine grit straight fissures and the plain fissure bur at both speed levels.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a high-speed bur in air rotor is not recommended for the preparation of tooth surfaces to be restored with composite resin restorations.
the type of bur used and speed of cutting teeth can influence the shear bond strength of composite resin to dentine.
the use of crosscut carbide burs, either in air rotors or in micromotors, may improve bonding for the adhesive systems used.
